proposed_urls.rationale: Section 39 - Definitions Applicable to Secs. 39 to 50 (lobbying-disclosure definitions).
Section 41 - Docket of Executive and Legislative Agents and Lobbyists; annual Registration; Identification Cards; Advisory Opinions.
Section 42 - Contingent-fee compensation for lobbying activity prohibited.
Section 43 - Executive and Legislative Agents; Itemized Statement of Expenditures; Notification of Legislators; Public Inspection; Family Gifts Restricted.
Section 44 - Registration of Organizations Attempting to Influence Legislation; Statement of Expenditures; Public Inspection; Penalty.
Section 45 - Inquiry and Adjudicatory Proceedings Relating to Alleged Violations of Secs. 39 to 50.
Section 46 - Docket of Executive and Legislative Agents; Maintenance; Legislative Year.
Section 47 - Employers of Executive or Legislative Agents; Statement of Expenditures; Filing; Penalty; Public Inspection.
Section 48 - Violation of Secs. 41 to 44 or 47 Respecting Executive or Legislative Agents; Penalties; Prosecutions; Enforcement.
Section 49 - Proceedings to Compel Filing of Proper Statement Required by Secs. 43, 44 or 47; equitable or Mandamus Relief to Enforce Secs. 41 to 43.
Section 50 - Sections Inapplicable to Public Employees or Agents or Other Persons Requested to Appear Before Committee or Commission (scope/exemption clause for lobbying regime).

notes: MA 2025 vintage available on Justia. Pass-1 selected Part I (chapters 1-182, Administration of the Government). MA tree is 5 levels deep: state -> part -> title -> chapter -> section. An intermediate pass-2 fetch was required at part-i/title-i/ before reaching c. 3. Pass-3 fetch on chapter-3/ returned a populated section list (per-section leaf convention), so each section URL is proposed individually. Proposed 11 sections (sections 39 and 41-50; section 40 is repealed and absent from the chapter index, consistent with the 2015 ground truth that the regime spans M.G.L. c. 3 ss. 39-50 minus s. 40). The Election Code (Title VIII, separate campaign-finance regime) was intentionally excluded; only Part I -> Title I -> c. 3 houses the lobbying-disclosure statute.
